raw_case_text: A 22-year-old woman presented to our hospital with pain abdomen and vomiting for 5 days. There was no history of fever, loose stools, dysuria, and hematuria on admission. Examination revealed distended abdomen and diffuse abdominal tenderness. She was oliguric on presentation and her serum creatinine was 2.6 mg%. She had leukocytosis (total count - 27,200 cells/cumm) with evidence of acute pancreatitis (serum lipase levels - 5250 U/L). Ultrasonogram (USG) showed enlarged pancreas with peripancreatic collections and it was confirmed on computed tomography (CT) of abdomen. There was no evidence of cholelithiasis on CT scan; however, omental inflammatory stranding with micronodular appearance was reported. She was managed conservatively with bowel rest and parenteral antibiotics. In view of oliguric renal failure, she was initiated on hemodialysis. She had normal triglyceride levels (94 mg/dl), and there was no evidence of sepsis (blood and urine cultures were sterile); however, her serum calcium level was high (12.8 mg/dl). Since no other cause was found, hypercalcemia was considered to be the cause for acute pancreatitis. USG neck was normal. Her parathyroid hormone (PTH) level was normal (18.73 IU/L), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D was 93 nmol/L, which ruled out hypervitaminosis D. However, 1, 25-dihydroxyvitamin D level was high (318 pmol/L). Calcium remained high in spite of dialysis, and she was treated with calcitonin injections. Serum angiotensin-converting enzyme level was normal (35 U/L). Whole-body positron emission tomography-CT (PET-CT) was done which showed a lesion with high fluorodeoxyglucose uptake in the terminal ileum [Figure 1a] and mesenteric lymph nodes. CT chest was normal. Colonoscopy showed mucosal nodularity with an ulcer and mild luminal narrowing in the terminal ileum. Biopsy samples were taken from the ileal ulcer and from the mesenteric lymph nodes using endoscopic ultrasound. Lymph node biopsy showed necrosis with noncaseating granuloma containing Langhans giant cells [Figure 1b], and biopsy from the ileal mucosa showed multiple discrete and large nonconfluent granulomas composed of epithelioid histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells; some of the granulomas showed central suppuration [Figure 1c]. Acid-fast bacilli were seen in the tissue. GeneXpert test from the tissue for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex was positive, and QuantiFERON TB gold assay was positive. After confirming tuberculosis, she was started on four-drug antituberculous therapy (ATT) at a modified dose. She was continued on hemodialysis as she was oliguric. In view of nonrecovery of renal function after 2 weeks, renal biopsy was done, which showed patchy cortical necrosis with fibrinoid necrosis of the medium-sized arteries [Figure 2a-c]. Antinuclear antibody and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody were negative, and serum complement level was normal. Two months after starting ATT, serum calcium level reduced to 9.1 mg/dl and 1, 25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels reduced to 18.16 pmol/L. Her urine output improved and was given a trial of dialysis withdrawal; however, she developed uremic symptoms and is dialysis dependent at the end of 6 months. The patient had hypercalcemia-induced acute severe pancreatitis which led to acute RCN and severe renal failure requiring dialysis. The cause of hypercalcemia is increased secretion of 1, 25-dihydroxyvitamin D from the granulomatous tissue in the terminal ileum, which is secondary to tuberculosis. The laboratory parameters of the patient before and after ATT have been depicted in Table 1.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 22-year-old woman presented with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain, vomiting, and oliguria.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Over the 5 days prior to admission, the patient developed acute diffuse abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, and decreased urine output without fever or diarrhea.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for abdominal pain, vomiting, and oliguria; negative for fever, loose stools, dysuria, or hematuria.

objective.physical_examination: Oliguric, distended abdomen with diffuse abdominal tenderness.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 27,200/mm^3, serum creatinine 2.6 mg/dL, markedly elevated serum lipase (5,250 U/L), hypercalcemia with serum calcium 12.8 mg/dL, normal triglycerides (94 mg/dL), normal intact PTH (18.73 IU/L), normal 25-hydroxyvitamin D (93 nmol/L), markedly elevated 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (318 pmol/L), normal serum ACE (35 U/L), negative ANA and ANCA, normal complement levels, sterile blood/urine cultures, and positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold assay. Neck ultrasound was normal; abdominal ultrasound showed an enlarged pancreas with peripancreatic fluid collections.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT confirmed acute pancreatitis with peripancreatic collections, no gallstones, and micronodular omental inflammatory stranding; chest CT was normal. Whole-body 18F-FDG PET-CT demonstrated intense FDG uptake in the terminal ileum and mesenteric lymph nodes. Colonoscopy and EUS-guided biopsies of a terminal ileal ulcer/nodularity and mesenteric lymph nodes revealed necrotizing/suppurative granulomas with epithelioid histiocytes, Langhans giant cells, positive tissue AFB staining, and positive tissue GeneXpert MTB/RIF. Percutaneous renal biopsy at week 2 for persistent oliguria showed patchy acute renal cortical necrosis (RCN) with medium-vessel fibrinoid necrosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Terminal ileal and mesenteric lymph node biopsies (granulomas with Langhans giant cells, positive AFB stain, and positive GeneXpert MTB/RIF) and a positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold test confirmed ileocecal and mesenteric tuberculous lymphadenitis causing ectopic calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D 318 pmol/L)-mediated severe hypercalcemia (12.8 mg/dL), acute severe pancreatitis, and biopsy-proven patchy acute renal cortical necrosis. Treatment with renal-dosed 4-drug anti-tuberculous therapy and calcitonin normalized her serum calcium (9.1 mg/dL) and calcitriol (18.16 pmol/L) within 2 months, though irreversible cortical necrosis left her on maintenance hemodialysis at 6 months.
